meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('white').

examples.trans: Vika has a white car.
The white one?
The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: Comparative: ближе. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('close, near').

examples.trans: We have grown closer.
This is my close friend.

examples.text: Слушайте, Марина, мы с вами стали ближе!
examples.trans: Listen, Marina, the two of us have grown closer!

meanings.note: Relating to Buddhism. Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('Buddhist').

examples.trans: And for insurance, a Buddhist temple too!

examples.text: В горах находится старый буддийский монастырь.
examples.trans: An old Buddhist monastery is located in the mountains.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'villa' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A villa in Monaco.

examples.text: Вилла в Монако, в Швейцарии счёт.
examples.trans: A villa in Monaco, an account in Switzerland.

examples.text: Они арендовали красивую виллу на лето.
examples.trans: They rented a beautiful villa for the summer.

meanings.note: Pointing at something. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.
Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There, look.
Here's my toy car.
All right, here you go. There, look.

вот-вот.gloss: just about, any minute, almost here

meanings.en: any minute now, right on the verge
meanings.note: Expresses imminent occurrence.

examples.trans: Happiness is getting closer, almost here!
The train will arrive any minute now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Come on, everything is fine.
Come on, that is all.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

выгореть.gloss: to burn out; (slang) to pan out, succeed

meanings.note: Literal. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'гореть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to burn out; (slang) to pan out, succeed', paired with 'выгорать'.

meanings.en: to pan out, succeed, pay off (colloquial)
meanings.note: Дело выгорело = the deal succeeded. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'гореть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to burn out; (slang) to pan out, succeed', paired with 'выгорать'.

examples.trans: If it doesn't pan out here, it will pan out there!
This risky plan finally paid off.

meanings.note: Дай! = give (me)!. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.trans: Give me just one.
Some water, please.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: I have no money.
The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.
This is for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.
Ещё больше = even more. Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You've still got some.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is my wife.

examples.text: Но вечером я обещал быть с женой.
examples.trans: But I promised to be with my wife this evening.

meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm here.
We live here.
But we're in business here.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'painting, picture' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У вас очень плохая картина по безопасности.
examples.trans: You have a very bad picture regarding safety.

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: female partner in an extramarital relationship

examples.trans: A supermodel wife and a mistress too.

examples.text: Он скрывал свою любовницу от семьи.
examples.trans: He hid his mistress from the family.

meanings.note: Feminine 3rd-declension noun. Common feminine noun meaning 'mosque' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A church, a mosque, and a synagogue are built.

examples.text: Рядом с рынком построили новую мечеть.
examples.trans: They built a new mosque next to the market.

meanings.note: after numbers: два миллиона, пять миллионов

examples.trans: Where's your forty million?

examples.text: Значит, предложение такое. Ты мне говоришь, где твои сорок миллионов.
examples.trans: So, here's the offer. You tell me where your forty million is.

meanings.note: На море = at/to the seaside. Common neuter noun meaning 'sea' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea!

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It needs a wash.
We need to do even more.
It needs a wash!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.
I'm a bit tired.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.en: to sail, swim, glide across water
meanings.note: плыть по морю = to sail across the sea

examples.trans: A white yacht sails across the sea.

examples.text: Мы с Лёней тогда плыли на ней.
examples.trans: Lyonya and I were sailing on it then.

meanings.note: In 'по поводу' + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'along; by; about' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'строить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to build', paired with 'строить'.

We will build the cluster.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'synagogue' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В старом районе открылась отреставрированная синагога.
examples.trans: A restored synagogue opened in the old district.

meanings.note: + genitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: So much gum!
How much is it?
So much gum! Cool!

meanings.note: + instrumental: стал сентиментальным
+ infinitive. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to become', paired with 'становиться'.

examples.trans: He became mayor.
You've changed.

examples.text: Ты слишком сентиментальным стал. А лидер должен быть жёстким.
examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.

meanings.note: для страховки = just to be safe, as insurance

examples.trans: And for insurance, a Buddhist temple too!

examples.text: Перед поездкой он оформил медицинскую страховку.
examples.trans: Before the trip he took out medical insurance.

meanings.note: Сч is pronounced like щ. Qualitative adjective formed with the productive suffix '-тельный'/'-ливый'. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('happy; lucky').
Qualitative adjective formed with the productive suffix '-тельный'/'-ливый'. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('happy; lucky').
Счастливый конец = happy ending. Qualitative adjective formed with the productive suffix '-тельный'/'-ливый'. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('happy; lucky').

examples.trans: I'm very happy.
The film has a happy ending.

examples.text: Ты сейчас один против всех. Счастливого конца не будет.
examples.trans: Right now you're alone against everyone. There won't be a happy ending.

meanings.note: К счастью = fortunately. Common neuter noun meaning 'happiness' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: For happiness.
How much money is needed for happiness?

examples.text: Сколько миллионов нужно человеку для счастья?
examples.trans: How many millions does a person need for happiness?

meanings.note: Счёт в банке. Common masculine noun meaning 'account, bill, score' in everyday Russian.
In a restaurant. Common masculine noun meaning 'account, bill, score' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Or a bank account.
Bring the bill, please.

examples.text: Или счёт в банке. Потому что они все обманщики.
examples.trans: Or a bank account. Because they are all cheats.

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Everything's fine there.
Who's there?
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'too, also' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

examples.trans: I was only looking.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ending in -ь. Common feminine noun meaning 'supermodel' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A supermodel wife and a mistress too.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?

I'm already home.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'temple, cathedral' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And for insurance, a Buddhist temple too!

examples.text: На вершине холма стоит древний храм.
examples.trans: An ancient temple stands atop the hill.

examples.text: Ну ничего, я потом построю храм.
examples.trans: Well, no matter, I will build a church later.

meanings.note: feminine noun; fleeting vowel drops in oblique forms: церкви, церквей

meanings.en: a little bit, just a little
meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'a little bit, slightly' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Core Russian num meaning 'six' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Nine, six, six.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'yacht' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A white yacht sails across the sea.

examples.text: В порту стояла огромная белая яхта.
